stops.name: Fiume, the tree-house, the eagle named Guido, the naked yogi
stops.campa: In Fiume Keller builds himself a small house in a tree and sleeps there, almost always half-naked, his trained Dinaric eagle, also named Guido, perched beside him. He walks the beach unclothed, exposes himself in gardens to scandalise the settled, keeps a blind Dalmatian ass and lives in what he calls the house of Diogenes. Hashish and cocaine, Vedanta and the sun: the ace has become a yogi-anarchist. D'Annunzio, delighted, once kidnaps the eagle as a prank, and must swiftly give it back.

stops.name: Fiume, the founding of Yoga with Comisso
stops.campa: With the young writer Giovanni Comisso, his companion and lover, with whom he shares a hotel, Keller founds Yoga, an Union of Free Spirits tending toward perfection, and its journal of the same name. It is no party but a brotherhood of holy pranksters and eretici, esoteric and naturist, taking even the ancient swastika for a solar sign. Within the pirate-republic Keller makes a still wilder republic of the spirit: the freest cell of the freest city, where poetry, action and the East are declared the only politics worth the name.
stops.quote: Un'Unione di spiriti liberi tendenti alla perfezione.

stops.name: Fiume airfield, the take-off in the SVA
stops.campa: Two days after Italy signs the Treaty of Rapallo, surrendering Fiume, Keller answers with the purest gesture the pirate-republic ever made. On 14 November 1920 he takes off in his Ansaldo SVA and points it at the capital, carrying red roses, a white rose, a bundle of carrots and turnips, and an enamelled chamber-pot. He will speak to Rome not in words but in objects: love to the people, contempt to the government. It is Fiume itself made flesh and set flying: a Dada raid before the word exists.

stops.name: The Vatican, the white rose for Frate Francesco
stops.campa: Over the Vatican Keller lets fall a single white rose, not for the Pope but for Frate Francesco, Brother Francis, the saint of the birds and of holy poverty. The gesture is entirely his: he salutes not the Church of power but the Franciscan spirit, the mendicant who owned nothing and loved everything. From the yogi-anarchist above St Peter's it is a benediction offered to the poorest, freest Christianity, one wanderer of the air blessing another who once walked barefoot through Umbria.
stops.quote_source: Guido Keller, dedication dropped over the Vatican, 14 November 1920

stops.name: The Quirinale, red roses for the Queen and the people of Italy
stops.campa: Over the Quirinal Keller drops seven red roses, dedicated to the Queen and to the people of Italy, a pledge of love to the nation, offered above the palace of its King. To the crown and the folk he brings flowers; the poison he reserves for the elected men who have signed away Fiume. In the theatre of his flight the roses are the whole of Italy that Keller still loves, kept carefully apart from the Parliament he is about to insult with all the splendour of his contempt.
stops.quote: Alla regina e al popolo d'Italia.
stops.quote_source: Guido Keller, dedication dropped over the Quirinale, 14 November 1920

stops.name: Montecitorio, the chamber-pot on the Parliament
stops.campa: Over the Palazzo di Montecitorio, seat of the Parliament, Keller drops an enamelled iron chamber-pot, hung with a bundle of yellow carrots and turnips and a message: the allegorical tangibility of their worth, handed to a government that governs by lies and by fear. The pitale misses the Chamber and lands on the roof of the Hotel Milan; no matter. The gesture is complete, indelible, pure Fiume: the pirate-republic of poets has answered the Treaty of Rapallo by defecating, symbolically and from the sky, upon the state.
stops.quote: Guido Keller, Ala Azione nello splendore, dona al Parlamento e al Governo che si reggono da tempo con la menzogna e con la paura, la tangibilità allegorica del Loro Valore. Roma, 14 del terzo mese della Reggenza.
stops.quote_source: Guido Keller, message attached to the chamber-pot dropped on Montecitorio, 14 November 1920

stops.name: San Marino, the forced landing and the improvised embassy
stops.campa: Bad weather forces Keller down at the ancient free republic of San Marino, and the little state receives the aviator as a hero. Never at a loss, he improvises there a message from d'Annunzio to the Italian government and secures diplomatic credentials that let him slip back through the blockade to Fiume. The eagle of the Quarnaro, having dropped roses and merde upon Rome in a single morning, comes home protected by the papers of the oldest republic in the world. The whole flight has the logic of a dream, and the audacity of a myth.

stops.name: Fiume, the Natale di sangue, the Christmas of Blood
stops.campa: At Christmas 1920 the Italian army, enforcing Rapallo, turns its guns on Fiume. The Natale di sangue, the Christmas of Blood, breaks the pirate-republic; a shell strikes the Governor's Palace itself and d'Annunzio yields to spare the city. Keller's dream ends where it lived, on the Quarnaro. Sixteen months of poetry and piracy, of eagles and chamber-pots and free unions of the spirit, close under artillery. The Comandante will withdraw to Lake Garda; his Segretario d'Azione will wander the earth, carrying Fiume with him like an incurable wound.

stops.name: Rome: the March, and the fascism that distrusted him
stops.campa: Restless after Fiume, Keller joins the fascist movement and takes part in the March on Rome of October 1922, yet the regime distrusts the heretic, and he it. He is too free, too mocking, too much the anarchist for the order the Blackshirts are building. The pirate of the Quarnaro cannot be domesticated into a functionary of the state he once dropped a chamber-pot upon. He is a man of one city and one dream, and that city has fallen; everything after is a search for something the century will not give him.

stops.name: Berlin, the aeronautical attaché
stops.campa: Keller returns to military flying and is sent to Berlin as aeronautical attaché to the Italian embassy. The ace who slept in a tree wears now the correct dress of a diplomat of the air. But the schemes and visions do not leave him: he dreams of aviation ventures, of new frontiers, of some impossible enterprise that might be Fiume again. The northern capital cannot hold the man of the Quarnaro any more than Milan could. He is always, everywhere, looking past the horizon for the republic that vanished.

stops.name: Benghazi, the desert flights over Libya
stops.campa: Keller flies over Libya, in the operations against the rebel tribes of Cyrenaica, the ace at war again, now above the desert instead of the Piave. But even the sands cannot fix him. The vision that drives him is not conquest but flight itself, the pure act, the splendour of action. He seeks in the empty sky what Fiume once gave him whole: a place where the free spirit might act without the ledger, the schoolmaster or the treaty. Libya is a station on a road that leads always outward, never home.

stops.name: The Amazon and Peru, up the great river, prospecting for gold
stops.campa: Keller crosses to South America and goes up the Amazon, visits Venezuela, and works in Peru as a prospector for gold. The Milanese aristocrat, the ace, the yogi, the pirate, is now a seeker in the green immensity, one of the atlas's wanderers who chase in far places the thing that eluded them at home. He finds no gold that holds. The eagle of Fiume has become a solitary figure on strange rivers, spending the last of a fortune and a legend on schemes that always dissolve into the next horizon.
